newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's D-Pharm raises $6 million in placement.
newsitem.headline: Israel's D-Pharm raises $6 million in placement.

text.p: D-Pharm, a company developing novel drugs based on a proprietary delivery system, said on Thursday it had completed a $6 million private placement.
The proceeds will be used to fund the accelerated development of drugs to treaty epilepsy, cardiac ischemia, brain stroke, cancer and viral diseases, the company said in a statement.

The shares were placed with two Israeli venture capital funds -- Apax-Leumi Israel Growth Fund, affiliated with British-based Apax Partners, and Vertex Venture Capital, affiliated with Singapore Technologies. The U.S.-based MedMax Ventures also took part.

D-Pharm, founded in 1993 and based in Rehovot outside Tel Aviv, is developing drugs based on its proprietary regulated activation of prodrugs (RAP) platform. RAP enables drugs to be activated only within the cells affected by disease, which reduces adverse side effects, the company said.
D-Pharm said it planned to complete pre-clinical development of DP-VPA, an epilepsy treatment this year, and begin clinical trials in 1998.
